Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu says the Nigeria Police Force is fully prepared to secure the 2027 elections, even if they were to start immediately.

He said the force has intensified training and retraining of officers to handle election security professionally, drawing lessons from recent off-cycle elections, and is working with the Army, the Civil Defence Corps, Customs, Immigration and the DSS.

A visiting partner urged the police to stay neutral and professional during the elections, warning against actions that could undermine public confidence.

The assurance came days before a wave of attacks on campaign events in several states, which the IGP has since promised to investigate.

items.author: m6
items.title: Sokoto government seals building used by ADC, citing security and unclear ownership
items.body:
The Sokoto State Government has sealed a building on Ahmadu Bello Way that the ADC and other parties had used, citing security concerns.

Commissioner for Lands and Housing Nasiru Dantsoho said records name the defunct Savannah Bank as the owner, with no documented transfer, and that the government has asked the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) to clarify ownership.

Atiku's campaign spokesperson, Phrank Shaibu, accepted that the bank owned the property but challenged the government's authority to close it, saying parties had used it for about two decades, most recently the PDP. He said he visited on Tuesday morning and met no physical restriction, and that the campaign had reported threats to the police, DSS and Civil Defence.

ADC National Publicity Secretary Bolaji Abdullahi warned the state government not to interfere with opposition campaigns.

items.author: m6
items.title: Sowore and supporters protest at police headquarters over Ado-Ekiti incident; 11 arrested
items.body:
Omoyele Sowore, the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, and his supporters protested at the police headquarters in Abuja, demanding prosecution of those who attacked his team at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti on the night of Friday, 30 October.

Sowore accused security personnel of involvement. The AAC rejected the police's description of the incident as an altercation, alleged government involvement, and called for an independent inquiry and the release of CCTV footage.

Ekiti police spokesperson Abutu Sunday said 11 suspects were arrested in Atikankan at about 10 p.m. that Friday, and that investigators are working out each suspect's role. The police statement did not name any political sponsor or establish who was responsible. The SSS said it is waiting for the police findings.

ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar also condemned the incident and called for an investigation.

items.author: m6
items.title: ADC lawyers ask INEC to hold off on implementing judgment that voided Atiku's nomination
items.body:
Lawyers for the ADC have asked INEC not to implement the judgment that voided Atiku Abubakar's presidential nomination until their appeal is decided.

Their letter, dated 6 November and stamped as received by the INEC chairman's office the same day, says the party has filed a notice of appeal and an application for a stay. Counsel Shaibu Enejoh Aruwa (SAN) noted that the Federal High Court had not yet heard the stay motion.

Justice Peter Lifu ruled that the David Mark-led caretaker leadership was unlawfully constituted and told INEC to disregard decisions of the party's 99th National Executive Committee meeting and later acts, including its presidential, governorship and legislative nominations. The claimant, Nafiu Bala Gombe, argues the party constitution made him the rightful successor to former chairman Ralph Nwosu.

No stay order had been confirmed as of Friday night, and the suit number in the letter differs from the one in an earlier ruling in the case.

items.author: m6
items.title: ADC state chairmen forum asks INEC to reopen nomination portal, threatens protests
items.body:
Kennedy Odion, secretary of the ADC NEC Chairmen Forum, has asked INEC to reopen its nominations portal so the party can submit names after any fresh primaries. The forum, which backs the faction that won the court case, threatened nationwide protests if INEC does not act.

INEC, meanwhile, disowned a viral poster claiming it had reaffirmed David Mark's leadership, saying the poster misused its logo and a photo of National Commissioner Mohammed Kudu Haruna. Haruna said the commission had not received a certified copy of the judgment and had not discussed the case.

As of Saturday, 7 November, INEC's party directory still listed Mark as national chairman and Rauf Aregbesola as national secretary.

The competing demands leave INEC between an appeal by the Mark-led leadership and pressure from the faction that won at the trial court.

items.author: m6
items.title: YPP running mate says opposition parties must agree a written programme before any joint ticket
items.body:
Patience Key, the Young Progressives Party's (YPP) vice-presidential candidate, says opposition parties considering a joint ticket should first agree on how they would govern.

She proposed a written programme stating what the parties would fund, who would carry it out, and when voters could expect results, to be agreed before the parties choose a common candidate.

Her proposal turns the usual coalition debate around: instead of starting with who leads, it starts with a shared plan.

With 18 presidential candidates on the January ballot, talk of opposition alliances continues, but no joint ticket has been formed.

items.author: m6
items.title: Fact-check: viral photo of 'massive' APC crowd in Kaduna was AI-generated
items.body:
A Facebook user shared an image said to show a huge crowd of supporters at an APC campaign rally in Kaduna State ahead of the 2027 elections, and many users shared it as evidence of the party's growing mobilisation.

The fact-checking organisation DUBAWA examined the image and found that it was generated with artificial intelligence.

AI-made crowd pictures are spreading for all parties. Before sharing a rally photo, check whether reliable outlets carried it, look for odd details such as warped faces, signs or limbs, and run a reverse image search.

items.author: m6
items.title: Kebbi inaugurates APC campaign council; Jigawa governor promises two million votes
items.body:
Kebbi Governor Nasir Idris inaugurated the APC's state campaign council on Sunday, days after Atiku Abubakar campaigned in Birnin Kebbi. In 2023, Atiku won Kebbi with 285,175 votes to Tinubu's 248,088.

In neighbouring Jigawa, Governor Umar Namadi said the APC could deliver two million votes for President Tinubu in 2027.

For comparison, Jigawa cast 954,805 votes in total in the 2023 presidential election, when Tinubu won 421,390 there. A two-million target would need far higher turnout than 2023, not just a bigger share.

items.author: m6
items.title: In Dutse, Kwankwaso revisits failed 2023 alliance with Obi
items.body:
Campaigning for the NDC in Dutse, Jigawa State, vice-presidential candidate Rabiu Kwankwaso revisited his failure to reach an alliance with Peter Obi before the 2023 election.

In 2023 the two contested separately, Obi for the Labour Party and Kwankwaso for the NNPP. They now share the NDC presidential ticket.

Atiku Abubakar is still running separately on the ADC platform, so this pairing is only one of several opposition arrangements in the race.

items.author: m6
items.title: Gombe: APC to launch campaign on 14 November, calls Pantami's candidacy illegitimate
items.body:
The Gombe State APC says it will launch its governorship campaign on 14 November, as the PDP prepared a large rally for its candidate, former minister Isa Ali Pantami.

APC Publicity Secretary Usman Murtala said the party has set up its campaign council and committees, and will go from community to community on the record of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in roads, healthcare and security. He described Pantami as an illegitimate candidate and said he should await a court decision before campaigning.

INEC has cleared Pantami and listed him as the PDP's governorship candidate after reviewing his initial omission.

Pantami won the PDP ticket in May, saying Gombe has a poverty rate of about 74.5 per cent and that he would tackle it through education and smart agriculture. The APC candidate is Jamilu Gwamna.

items.author: m7
items.title: Imo: pro-Tinubu group warns Uzodimma–Okorocha Senate feud could hurt APC in the South-East
items.body:
The Renewed Hope Foot Soldiers for Tinubu, led by Gbenga Owojori, has warned that the dispute between Governor Hope Uzodimma and former governor Rochas Okorocha over the Imo West Senate ticket could weaken APC unity and hurt President Tinubu's campaign in the South-East.

The warning followed a Federal High Court ruling directing the APC to submit Okorocha's name as its candidate for Imo West. The group argued that Uzodimma should also have a fair chance to pursue his Senate ambition.

Uzodimma's camp has announced plans to challenge the judgment. It was not confirmed that an appeal had been filed or that the ruling had been stayed.

items.author: m7
items.title: Bayelsa: PDP and APC chairmen clash over Governor Diri's role in Tinubu campaign
items.body:
Bayelsa PDP chairman George Turnah has questioned Governor Douye Diri's participation in President Tinubu's campaign activities, after the governor's move from the PDP to the APC.

The state APC chairman, Warman Weri Ogoriba, rejected the criticism, saying the governor has shown his support through public engagements.

The exchange reflects how the governor's defection has reshaped Bayelsa politics, with former governor Seriake Dickson now leading the NDC and the PDP left without the state government behind it.

items.author: m7
items.title: Atiku and APC clash over Tinubu's electricity record; Atiku proposes ending tariff bands
items.body:
ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has challenged the APC's defence of President Tinubu's electricity record and proposed replacing the tariff-band system with pricing tied to the electricity customers actually receive.

APC spokesperson Dele Alake said Tinubu's pledge on power should be read together with his undertaking to explain any shortfall before seeking a second term. The APC pointed to the Electricity Act 2023, metering, transmission investment, state regulatory reforms and a ₦4 trillion bond to settle verified legacy power-sector debts, and said over 1.5 million customers have been metered.

Atiku's spokesperson, Phrank Shaibu, said homes and businesses remain in darkness despite the paperwork. Atiku said Band A customers often paid about ₦209.50 per kWh before VAT despite unreliable supply, and questioned the reported plan to end subsidies from 2027.

His proposal came without a tariff formula, subsidy plan or cost estimate.

items.author: m7
items.title: Rivers: APC and NDC candidates explain why they missed citizens' charter signing
items.body:
Five governorship candidates in Rivers State signed a 13-point Citizens' Charter of Demands organised by the Rivers Peace Initiative, but the APC candidate, Kingsley Chinda, and the NDC candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, did not attend. Both are seen as frontline contenders.

APC spokesperson Chibike Ikenga said Chinda was not invited and questioned the organisers' process. An ally of Chinda said she did not know whether he received an invitation, and described the charter as not binding on the people of the state.

The NDC campaign's spokesperson said Lulu-Briggs had a party rally in Yenagoa, Bayelsa, the same day, and declined to send his deputy instead.

The convener, Obinna Ebogidi, said invitations went to all candidates, and that both can still sign separately. Neither campaign said it opposes the charter.

items.author: m7
items.title: Kano: INEC says court order stops it publishing NDC governorship ticket
items.body:
INEC has cited a Federal High Court order to explain why it cannot publish the names of the NDC's Kano governorship candidate, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, and his running mate, Mustapha Kwankwaso.

The pair were missing from the governorship list INEC published on 10 October. The NDC said officials initially blamed a computer problem. A suit (FHC/KN/CS/440/2026) was later filed by three party members against INEC and the NDC, and Justice Samuel Amobeda issued an interim order restraining publication pending further hearing. INEC has acknowledged that Gwarzo met its nomination requirements, and its updated list marks both NDC slots as 'Court Order'.

Gwarzo questions why his name was missing before the order existed. The NDC has gone to the Federal High Court in Abuja to compel INEC to list its ticket and plans to challenge the Kano order.

Rabiu Kwankwaso accused the APC and allies of Governor Abba Yusuf of trying to exclude the ticket. Kano APC chairman Umar Doguwa denied this, calling it an internal NDC dispute.

items.author: m7
items.title: Rivers: Wike tells Lulu-Briggs' kinsmen their son cannot win under the NDC
items.body:
FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has told the people of Abonnema, home community of the NDC governorship candidate in Rivers State, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, that their son cannot win the 2027 election on the NDC platform.

Speaking at a town hall meeting in Abonnema, Akuku-Toru Local Government Area, on Thursday, Wike said he understood their wish to see their son become governor but urged them to be realistic. He asked them to back the APC candidate, Kingsley Chinda, noting that Chinda's running mate is also from their community.

The NDC has not responded to the remarks. Lulu-Briggs is among 19 governorship candidates INEC cleared in Rivers.

items.author: m7
items.title: INEC raises alarm over plot to kidnap election workers; suspects charged
items.body:
INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says intelligence operations uncovered a plot to threaten, intimidate and kidnap ad hoc election staff, including NYSC members, ahead of the 2027 elections.

Speaking at the North-Central zonal readiness assessment in Lokoja, he said suspected masterminds were arrested and taken to court through the DSS, and warned that anyone who threatens or harms election personnel will face the full weight of the law. He also warned INEC staff against partisan conduct and negligence.

Amupitan said credible elections cannot be achieved through last-minute arrangements, and that INEC is working with security agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security.

INEC expects to manage over 103 million registered voters across 176,846 polling units. The final register will be published on 15 December after corrections.

items.author: m7
items.title: Atiku says he is staying in the race; APC denies any role in the ADC court case
items.body:
In a statement dated 6 November, Atiku Abubakar said he remains in the 2027 presidential race and that his campaign will keep its focus on food prices, fuel costs and insecurity.

He accused the Tinubu administration of using the courts to limit electoral competition, but offered no evidence of influence. ADC spokesperson Bolaji Abdullahi said the party will keep its campaign organisation in place.

APC National Publicity Secretary Felix Morka denied that his party had any role in the case. He said the suit grew out of an internal ADC dispute over how the Mark-led group took control, and urged the ADC to appeal and settle its leadership crisis.

INEC's published candidate list still names Atiku and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, while the appeal is pending.

items.author: m7
items.title: Fact-check: no evidence for claim that Tinubu met INEC chairman in France
items.body:
NNPP chieftain Buba Galadima alleged on Channels Television's Politics Today that President Tinubu held a private meeting in France with the INEC chairman and other prominent Nigerians, and suggested it could have implications for the 2027 elections.

DUBAWA found no evidence to support the allegation.

Galadima also claimed that Nigerians aged 18 to 35 make up 65 per cent of registered voters, describing them as a major voting bloc. Young people are a large share of the register, but exact proportions depend on INEC's published breakdown, which voters can check.

INEC has repeatedly said it has no candidate and no party in the election.

items.author: m7
items.title: APC campaign proposes 3 December to inaugurate Kaduna–Kano and Kano–Maradi rail sections
items.body:
The APC Presidential Campaign Council has proposed 3 December as the date to inaugurate two rail sections: the 190 km Jaji–Kano section of the Kaduna–Kano railway, and the 250 km Dawanu–Kano–Kazaure–Daura–Katsina section of the Kano–Maradi line.

The council put completion at about 90 per cent for Kaduna–Kano and 70 per cent for Kano–Maradi. The transport ministry had earlier named December as its commissioning target.

An inauguration does not confirm when regular passenger services will begin. The proposed date is about six weeks before the 16 January presidential election.

items.author: m7
items.title: House of Reps sets up committee to probe attacks on political rallies, report due in three weeks
items.body:
The House of Representatives on Thursday, 12 November, adopted without debate a motion on rising violence during political campaigns, sponsored by Minority Leader Frederick Agbedi (PDP, Bayelsa) and 16 other lawmakers.

The House condemned violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property linked to political rallies, whatever the party, and urged parties and candidates to avoid inflammatory language and cooperate with security agencies.

The motion cited disrupted meetings in Enugu on 12 September, where one person was allegedly killed; an attack on APC supporters travelling to a Katsina rally on 28 October, after which 14 suspects were arrested; violence at an APC rally in Lafia, Nasarawa, on 4 November; and an attack on a procession in Asaba on 7 November that left one dead and five injured. Violence in Calabar was also raised.

A committee drawn from the Police Affairs and National Security committees, headed by a principal officer, will investigate the causes and report within three weeks. Agbedi warned against blaming anyone before impartial inquiries are complete.

items.author: m7
items.title: Tinubu orders security agencies to crack down on political thuggery
items.body:
President Bola Tinubu has directed security agencies to act against political violence ahead of the 2027 elections, in a State House statement issued on Friday, 13 November.

He said every party and candidate must be able to campaign anywhere in Nigeria without intimidation or threats, that his government will not tolerate conduct that threatens public order during the campaign, and he condemned all forms of campaign violence. He urged parties to campaign on policies and ideas and said rivals should not see each other as enemies.

The statement followed reports of attacks on an APC convoy in Funtua, Katsina, on 28 October; violence at an NDC procession in Asaba on 7 November that police said left one dead and five injured; and the disruption of an NDC town hall in Lagos on 12 November, alongside incidents in Ekiti, Cross River and Sokoto.

The police had warned a week earlier that people who attack opponents or destroy campaign materials would be arrested and prosecuted.
